Could we get some design docs up on what this is?  I see 8 binaries in https://github.com/AspeedTech-BMC/fmc_imgtool/tree/master/prebuilt

What are they, how are they used, and why are there 8?  I see one is a caliptra image, which is itself an open source project, why can't we build that from source?

I'm assuming it's from here: https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-sw

But with the way these are provided it's impossible to know.

These prebuilt binaries are used by `bootmcu-spl` to boot the AST2700.
We use fmc-imgtool to generate BOOTMCU_FW_BINARY = "ast2700-ibex-spl.bin
Refer to:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openbmc/+/81058/17/meta-aspeed/recipes-bsp/bootmcu/bootmcu-spl.inc#81

Please refer to the ASPEED SDK User Guide for information on these prebuilt binaries.

We plan to build `caliptra-sw` to generate the Caliptra image for AST2700 A2.
@ed@tanous.net Please let me know if my answer didn’t address your question.

>  Please let me know if my answer didn’t address your question.

No, it did not address "Could we get some design docs up on what this is?"

Also, there are 8 binaries in that link, you've still not documented where they came from, or why it can't be built from source.

> I just confirmed with our engineering team that the AST2700 A2 will continue to use a prebuilt Caliptra image.

Great!  Now please get alignment (through a design doc) with the OpenBMC project.  Your internal engineering teams do not set OpenBMC policy, and while I suspect many of us want to support the 2700 getting into the tree, opque binaries will likely need some consensus built, and some guidelines agreed to on how that's managed.  Keep in mind the "open" in openbmc refers to open source, so just dumping binaries into the build isn't something that's likely going to be allowed without documentation.


> On MP parts, the vendor key hash is fused in OTP. Therefore, without our private key, any image built from source cannot be authenticated

This is only if the build is not reproducible, which anything in that build SHOULD be reproducible.  If this is just a matter of checking in the aspeed signature, that can be built from verified source, that's very different than checking in the full binaries.

I added a design doc for AST27x0.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/85917

This should not be done.  You're including files from somewhere way else in the tree?  Can't you depend on the tool itself rather than doing this include?  What part of this tool repository are you using here?

Using [fmc-imgtool.inc](https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-aspeed/recipes-aspeed/python/fmc-imgtool.inc) lets us share the same SRC_URI/SRCREV with fmc-imgtool.bb. As I understand it, depend on cannot make two recipes share the same SRC_URI/SRCREV. If I’m wrong, please correct me.

The fmc-image_git.bb is used to install the prebuilt images from.
https://github.com/AspeedTech-BMC/fmc_imgtool/tree/master/prebuilt
